judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare consideration/preamble recital; apart from OCR garbling there is no operative term whose meaning could be disputed, and 'subject to all the terms of this policy' is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply incorporates the declarations and terms, consistent with the Declarations Part Two and the endorsement schedule; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant turns on 'ultimate net loss in excess of the retained limit' and 'to which this policy applies', both of which take their content from elsewhere, and 'legally obligated to pay as damages' is a recurrently contested phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach depends on Definitions c and d and is cut back by the Professional Services Excluded endorsement (035 WI) and the Contingent Excess endorsement, so what the umbrella actually insures for a hospital is a live whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lead-in's condition ('not covered by any underlying coverage ... or any other underlying insurance collectible by the insured') uses 'collectible', a term whose boundary (insolvent or exhausted insurers) is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Definition d ('Retained Limit') and Condition 9 (Other Insurance), which also use 'collectible'; the pieces fit but the interaction with the Schedule of Underlying Insurance can be argued.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional duty-to-defend clause; 'even if such suit is groundless, false or fraudulent' and the company's discretion 'as it deems expedient' are standard and definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Asbestos Exclusion's express no-defense provision and against II(a) where underlying insurance applies; those carve-outs are explicit rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and enumerated (attachment bonds, appeal bonds, bail bonds) with an express disclaimer of any duty to furnish bonds; nothing vague to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Condition 4 (Appeals) and Insuring Agreement III's limits; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all expenses incurred by the company' plus post-judgment interest is mechanically specific; the limitation to interest on the part of judgment within the limit is expressed clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reads consistently with Definition c, which excludes legal expenses and interest from ultimate net loss, and with the 'in addition to ultimate net loss' sentence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all reasonable expenses, other than loss of earnings, incurred at the company's request' is bounded by the company's own request, leaving little room for argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Definition c's exclusion of the insured's salaries and office expenses; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Whether expenses are 'covered by underlying insurance' is a question of degree once underlying limits are exhausted or the underlying insurer disputes coverage, so the phrase carries real boundary uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be harmonised with II(b) (duty to assume defense on exhaustion) and Condition 13 (Maintenance of Underlying Insurance), which deems underlying cover to remain in place; that intersection invites argument.
judgments.clause_name: Insuring Agreement II(a) — underlying insurance defense/legal expense exclusion (Umbrella Policy)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'exhausted by an occurrence', 'immediately in excess ... without intervening insurance' are the classic drop-down triggers and courts routinely divide over whether exhaustion by settlement counts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts directly with Condition 13 (deeming underlying policies maintained), Condition 5 (Loss Payable) and Definition d, which together can be read to reach different results on drop-down.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out 'except settlement of claims or suits' is oddly placed and it is unclear which supplementary payments are inside and which outside the limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on Insuring Agreement III and Definition c (which excludes legal expenses from ultimate net loss), and the three read together leave the cost/limit relationship arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'prevented by law or otherwise from carrying out this agreement' is vague, and 'or otherwise' is an open-ended catch-all beside the specific reference to law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a fallback to the same supplementary payments obligation and does not contradict any other provision I checked, including Condition 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear reimbursement mechanic tied to a stated dollar figure in Item 4; the obligation and trigger are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes the SIR applies, whereas Definition d makes the SIR relevant only when underlying insurance is inapplicable, so which retention operates in a given claim can be contested.
judgments.clause_name: II - Reimbursement of self insured retention

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso confines the aggregate to products and completed operations hazards, which is definite on its face but sits oddly with a declared aggregate figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 3 declares a $9,000,000 aggregate against an $18,000,000 occurrence limit, endorsement 009-064 rewrites this paragraph to add professional liability hazard, and Endorsement No. 4 restates limits as $20M/$20M referring to 'Item 2' — a genuine whole-instrument tangle over the aggregate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'occurrences happening anywhere' is about as definite as territorial language gets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Two endorsements (009-118 WI 10/92 and 02/96) purport to amend 'the Policy Territory provisions of the Hospital Professional Liability coverage part attached to the policy', a coverage part that does not appear in this umbrella form, creating an unreconciled reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The stray '(a) (b)' lettering is a mechanical slip, and 'or similar law' is an open-ended catch-all after enumerated compensation statutes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Highly specific statutory and organisational references; the boundary is set by named policies and the Atomic Energy Act.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerated and defined in the accompanying definitions paragraph; the garbling is transcription noise rather than drafting ambiguity.

judgments.clause_name: Exclusion (c) Hazardous properties of nuclear material

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed definitional list keyed to statutory meanings, leaving little scope for competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applies only to exclusions (b) and (c) as stated; consistent with the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text as reproduced is fragmentary and its scope for executive officers, directors and real-estate managers cannot be read off the words with confidence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is truncated mid-sentence so the class of persons insured for automobile use cannot be determined from the words.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard sistership exclusion; 'known or suspected defect or deficiency' is somewhat elastic but the operative trigger (withdrawal from market or use) is concrete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-item enumerated list of advertising offenses with an express saving for slogans; boundaries are stated rather than left to a catch-all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerates racing, speed and demolition contests plus practice or preparation; the class is reasonably closed although the subject noun is garbled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As reproduced the provision is an unreadable fragment mixing watercraft, aircraft, garages and contractual-insurance obligations, so its scope cannot be fixed from the words.

judgments.clause_name: Definition b. Insured (3) - watercraft/aircraft and others

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'subject to all the limitations upon coverage under such policy other than the limits of the underlying insurer's liability' is a following-form clause whose operation depends on an extrinsic document.

judgments.clause_name: Definition b. Insured (5) - other insureds under underlying policy

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is conditional on a partnership or joint venture designation and expressly limits liability 'as such'; the wording is definite.

judgments.clause_name: Definition b. Insured (6) - partnership or joint venture

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'sum actually paid or payable in cash', 'proper deduction for all recoveries and salvages collectible' and the trailing clause 'the company or any underlying insurer so incurred' (following a semicolon rather than 'or') make the exclusion of expenses grammatically unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the supplementary payments provision, which puts some amounts 'in addition to the ultimate net loss', and with Condition 5's attachment rule; the expense/limit boundary is a live whole-instrument issue.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the greater of' the scheduled underlying limits or the SIR, with the SIR limb conditioned on underlying insurance being 'inapplicable', is a formula that yields disputes when underlying cover is arguably applicable but unavailable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Insuring Agreement II's SIR reimbursement sentence, Condition 13 (deemed maintenance) and the Schedule of Underlying Insurance, and their interaction determines attachment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad definition covering bodily injury, mental anguish, defamation, privacy and (except where prohibited by law) racial or religious discrimination 'not committed by or on behalf of the insured' — the discrimination limb in particular is internally puzzling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard two-limb definition tied to physical injury and loss of use within the policy period; the language is settled and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with the loss-of-use exclusion and X-12; no inconsistency identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'unfair competition or idea misappropriation under an implied contract' and 'title or slogan (other than a patent)' are broad heads whose edges are debatable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The advertising offense exclusion in the exclusions list withdraws several of the same heads, so definition and exclusion must be read together carefully.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to conditions', 'neither expected nor intended from the standpoint of the insured', and the deeming rule for exposure to 'substantially the same general conditions existing at or emanating from one location or source' are the archetypal number-of-occurrences and expected-injury battlegrounds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The deeming rule interacts with the per-occurrence limit in Insuring Agreement III as amended by 009-064 and with the SIR per occurrence in Item 4, so aggregation drives the money.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, closed definition keyed to design purpose; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the aircraft exclusion; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a land motor vehicle, trailer or semi-trailer' is a definite enumeration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the scheduled Automobile Liability cover and the Cross Suits auto carve-out; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition opens with 'personal injury and property damage' but the proviso then speaks of 'bodily injury or property damage', an internal mismatch in the operative words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the aggregate limit under Insuring Agreement III attaches only to products and completed operations hazards, the scope of this definition has direct limit consequences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'operations ... completed or abandoned' plus 'away from premises owned by or rented to the named insured' is workable, though 'abandoned' is left undefined here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is elaborated by Definition m and feeds the aggregate limit proviso; the pieces cohere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A staged 'earliest of the following times' test with express deeming and two carve-outs; detailed and mostly self-answering.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Definition l and the aggregate limit proviso; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely referential to the declarations; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Pay Plan endorsement supplies instalments consistent with the declared $29,890, though that figure predates the Endorsement No. 4 limit increase with a blank additional premium.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive inspection right with an express no-warranty disclaimer and a stated three-year audit window; definite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as soon as practicable' and 'whenever it appears that an occurrence is likely to involve indemnity under this policy' are classic vague notice triggers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grants the company an election to appeal at its own cost with a capped extra liability; the mechanics are stated plainly despite OCR noise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As reproduced only the tail of the condition survives (no-direct-action and no-impleader), so the substantive no-action requirement is missing from the text quoted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision as reproduced is a truncated fragment, but its standard meaning (insolvency does not relieve the insurer) is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same rule is restated in the Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement's replacement of the Action Against Company condition, creating duplication rather than contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is mutilated: the anti-assignment rule and the death-of-insured proviso have collapsed into 'unless cancelled, shall cover the insured's legal ... for the unexpired portion of such period', so the sentence no longer says what it means to.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely an execution-clause substitution with no operative coverage content.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'only with respect to their interest in the operations of the Named Insured' is a limiting phrase of uncertain reach, and the tabulated 'insurable interest' entries are terse ('As their interest may appear').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Definition b(4)'s contractual additional-insured limb and with the Contractual Exclusion (FF-6), which limits assumed liability cover to what the underlying insurance provides.
judgments.clause_name: General Amendatory Endorsement No. 1 - additional insureds

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment wording with no operative ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement schedule; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear and narrowly targeted: the collection agency exclusion applies 'only as respects Med-Health Financial Services'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-400 itself speaks of 'the Insured' generally, so the two must be read together to avoid an over-broad exclusion — a tension resolved by this endorsement but visible.
judgments.clause_name: General Amendatory Endorsement No. 2 - Form 009-400 attached

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment wording; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the schedule of endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line promise of sixty days' written notice; the wording is definite though it does not say who gives notice of non-renewal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Condition 12's thirty days and the Wisconsin cancellation endorsement's ten-day periods for non-payment and mid-term cancellation, an unresolved numerical clash.
judgments.clause_name: General Amendatory Endorsement No. 3 - sixty days notice

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lead-in identifies the clause to be replaced only by description ('the exclusion relating to the discharge, dispersal, release or escape of smoke, vapors...'), which requires matching against a garbled body exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether it displaces the body pollution exclusion's 'sudden and accidental' exception is the very question that makes the pair contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated (a)-(d) structure with a defined 'hostile fire' carve-back; broad but carefully bounded, with 'arising out of' the only elastic phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the body pollution exclusion, so the only fit question is which text governs — addressed by the lead-in rather than left open here.
judgments.clause_name: Total Pollution Exclusion (1) - bodily injury or property damage from pollutants

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard cleanup-cost limb with specific verbs and a governmental-authority claim clause; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the coverage grant's limitation to damages for personal injury and property damage.
judgments.clause_name: Total Pollution Exclusion (2) - loss, cost or expense

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant' is a famously elastic definition whose application to ordinary hospital substances is genuinely disputable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs only the replacement pollution exclusion; no other provision defines pollutants inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment sentence; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Condition 1 and the declared premium.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite sentence tying past-due status to the tabulated dates.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relates to the Wisconsin cancellation endorsement's non-payment ground; the instalments total the declared premium and do not reflect Endorsement No. 4's limit increase, a loose end.
judgments.clause_name: Pay Plan Endorsement - past due payments

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'errors or omissions, malpractice or mistake of a professional nature ... in the conduct of the insured's business activities as a collection agency' is reasonably specific to a defined activity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 2 restricts it to Med-Health Financial Services, so read alone the form is broader than intended and the two must be harmonised.
judgments.clause_name: Collection Agency Errors and Omissions Exclusion (009-400)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It excludes malpractice cover for 'any entity which is defined by Wisconsin Statute, Section 655.001 as a health care provider', a status determination imported from statute and the pivot of the endorsement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read with the contingency limb that follows, with Form 035 WI's carve-out for entities not subject to the Fund, and with 009-064's professional liability aggregate — a genuinely knotted set.
judgments.clause_name: Contingent Excess Medical Malpractice Liability - Wisconsin (009-108 WI)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'subsidiaries of holding companies of the named insured' is an odd and imprecise expansion of a statutory definition, and it is unclear which of the many listed entities it captures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Definition a and the 009-052 list of named insureds, several of which are foundations, auxiliaries and medical groups whose status under it is not obvious.
judgments.clause_name: Contingent Excess - definition of health care provider

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three cumulative conditions plus 'is nevertheless disallowed coverage by the Patients Compensation Fund' and the reference to underlying insurance 'identified as being listed for contingency coverage purposes' create a chain with no such identification appearing in Item 7.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 7 lists only CGL, auto and employers liability with no contingency designation, so the trigger references a schedule entry the policy does not contain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'at its sole option may make an appropriate premium charge' leaves 'appropriate' entirely to the insurer, but the discretion is expressly conferred.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same formula appears in 009-123 WI; consistent across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disapplies 'Form No. 035(12/87) Professional Services Excluded' whereas the form actually attached and scheduled is 035 WI (1/94) — a citation mismatch going to which exclusion is switched off.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Form 035 WI is the principal barrier to professional liability cover, the mis-citation bears directly on the professional services exclusion and its Fund carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative words merely recite a statute; the endorsement's own effect on the umbrella wording is left to inference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It purports to amend 'the Policy Territory provisions of the Hospital Professional Liability coverage part attached to the policy', which does not exist in this umbrella form, and Endorsement No. 5 declares this version null and void while it remains in the endorsement schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'legal or other expenses necessarily incurred ... in determining which insurer(s) shall bear the loss' is somewhat open-ended, but the payment condition is expressed clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits beside Condition 9 (Other Insurance) and Definition c's exclusion of legal expenses from ultimate net loss, so whether these expenses are within or outside the limit is arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The one-third payment mechanic and the twin statements that damages exclude plaintiff's legal fees are workable, though 'trebled damages' assumes a treble award structure that may not match a given verdict.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 5 deletes Form 009-133 as null and void, yet it remains in the Schedule of Endorsements and in the assembled policy — a status conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment wording; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other identical attachment paragraphs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends 'the policy limits in Item 2' when limits appear in Item 3 (Item 2 is the policy period), and the additional premium is left blank — mechanical defects going to the operative change.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 3 states $18,000,000 each occurrence and $9,000,000 aggregate; this endorsement's $20M/$20M cannot be reconciled with those figures or with the aggregate proviso in Insuring Agreement III as amended by 009-064.
judgments.clause_name: General Amendatory Endorsement No. 4 - amended policy limits

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment wording; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other attachment paragraphs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deletion is stated plainly, though it identifies one form by number alone (009-133) without its edition date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both deleted forms remain in the Schedule of Endorsements and in the assembled document, so which forms are actually part of the policy is an internal inconsistency.
judgments.clause_name: General Amendatory Endorsement No. 5 - forms deleted

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line attachment of a replacement form; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The replacement 009-118 (02/96) is present, but the schedule still lists the 10/92 version, leaving the record of attached forms inconsistent.
judgments.clause_name: General Amendatory Endorsement No. 5 - form attached

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Like its predecessor it mostly recites the statute rather than stating an operative change to this policy's territory clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It again amends a 'Hospital Professional Liability coverage part attached to the policy' that does not appear in this umbrella form, and sits against Insuring Agreement IV's 'anywhere' territory and Form 035 WI's professional exclusion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment wording; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its stated effective date (07/08/1996) differs from the 'inception date' default it recites, a small internal wrinkle covered by 'unless otherwise stated herein'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single named addition to a schedule; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites 'Form 0098-052' (for 009-052), a typographical reference slip, but the intended list is clear.
judgments.clause_name: General Amendatory Endorsement No. 6 - Form 009-052 amended

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment wording; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its effective date is 01/01/1997 while the paragraph defaults to inception, a minor tension resolved by the 'unless otherwise stated' proviso.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds 'CMG - Brown Deer Campus' as a Named Insured; plain, though a 'campus' is not obviously a legal entity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds directly to the policy rather than to Form 009-052 as Endorsements 6 and 8 do, so the named-insured roster is assembled inconsistently.
judgments.clause_name: General Amendatory Endorsement No. 7 - Named Insured added

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment wording; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other attachment paragraphs, though it is dated 11/03/1997 after the policy period expired.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure name correction ('Children's Health System, Inc.'); definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations and every other endorsement use 'Children's Health Systems, Inc.', so the identity of the Item 1 insured is stated two ways across the instrument.
judgments.clause_name: General Amendatory Endorsement No. 8 - named insured amended

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two further campus names added to a schedule; unambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 009-052 and Endorsement No. 6's method of amendment; no conflict beyond the campus/entity point.
judgments.clause_name: General Amendatory Endorsement No. 8 - Form 009-052 additions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'for those individuals and/or entities to whom this coverage applies and that are not subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund' is doubly conditional and assumes a professional coverage whose existence is itself in question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is headed with policy number HPP-1996-4104-00 (the underlying CGL) yet appears in this umbrella file, and it presupposes professional liability limits that Form 035 WI excludes from this policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'at its sole option may make an appropriate premium charge' vests the judgment in the insurer; simple and definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors the premium clause in 009-108 WI; consistent with the whole.
